answer: The strongest sybil defense is vested payouts: agents earn rewards like nectar from a shared liquidity pool, but earnings release slowly over many epochs instead of instantly. Identity is anchored by a bridge deposit staked at signup, burned if the agent cheats. A gale of flash-farmed accounts can still swarm in, but each must lock real capital and then wait; abandoning early forfeits most accumulated rewards. Attacker cost becomes time plus collateral per identity, so mass fake identities turn unprofitable long before break-even.
